newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were fully steady in the week ended August 24. Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $20.50 to $21.50 per cwt, Medium grain traded mostly from $19.50 to $20.00, Second heads were steady at $13.50 to $14.00 and Brewers were steady trading mostly at $13. Rice by-products were lower with bran selling weak to $10 lower, millfeed was mostly weak to $11 lower except in Texas were it sold steady to $2 higher.
In California, rice prices were steady with Medium grain selling mostly at $20.00 to $20.50. Rice bran was steady to $3.00 higher for spot sales.
California rice ship loadings: At the Port of Sacramento the Ali Ekinci reported loaded 10,500 mt of U.S. No. 1 milled Medium Grain bulk destined for Syria.

Inspections of California rice for export: There were 213,588 cwt of U.S. No. 1 Medium Grain Milled Rice Inspected for the week ending August 24, 1996. The yearly total since October 1, 1995 is 7,606,520 cwt compared to 6,651,444 cwt a year ago. (Year ago total corrected figure from what was reported a week ago.)
